pairs.subject: agent-instruction-files
pairs.evidence: src/lib/llm/transport/claude.ts:155 Assessment runs launch `claude -p` from a neutral tmpdir, which keeps the project brief out by position, but no code captures or asserts which instruction files actually loaded and no --setting-sources or --bare flag is passed, so an operator's user-level brief would silently become an uncontrolled input to scan scores (none exists on this machine as of 2026-11-09).

techniques.evidence: src/lib/llm/transport/env-strip.test.ts:67 The positional fix is present, but the guard asserts the layout on a mocked spawn; the technique requires the isolation claim to be verified against what actually loaded, and a repo-wide search of src finds no loaded-set capture (no InstructionsLoaded, --setting-sources or --bare).
src/lib/llm/transport/types.ts:3 One child process per call means no clear, compaction or resume for a delivered copy to outlive.
src/lib/llm/claude-cli.ts:44 The instructions here are assembled per call by the application, which is prompt-assembly territory, not a repo-owned always-loaded floor.
src/lib/llm/transport/types.ts:1 The per-CLI contract normalizes spawning and results; it compiles no skill or instruction asset per host.

pairs.registryProposal: workspace-ancestry-isolation frames the span as an ancestry walk and says a sibling layout empties it by construction, but a launch outside every project tree still receives user-global instruction files and settings, which are not on the ancestry walk; the technique should name that layer and how to exclude or assert it.
